## Context

Designed under 475e-9b99-9085-4b2d (see its design comment for the full argument and Limits).

`llm/overlap/queue.py::_events_of` opens and `json.load`s EVERY matching event file, and
`reduce_ticket` calls it three times per ticket. `enrich_drain.maybe_drain` calls
`pending_enrichment` as its "cheap gate" on every write against a 20 ms budget
(`overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms`). Measured on this repo's live tracker (3,727 ticket dirs):
the gate does 11,181 `listdir` calls and 4,977 file opens per invocation, and logs
`enrich drain gate check took 404.9 ms (> 20 ms budget)` on every rebar command (observed
404-654 ms). The opens term grows without bound as enrichment re-runs accumulate; the budget
does not.

`digest_sidecar.latest_ticket_digest` is already bounded (sorts dirents, walks newest-first,
returns on the first parseable payload) and needs no change. This ticket is the queue side only.

## Plan

Make the queue reduce read newest-first and lazily, changing no on-disk behaviour.

The event filename is `{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json` where the prefix is the same monotonic
timestamp the reducer compares (`_store/event_append.py::event_filename`, built by
`_prepare_event` from the validated event's own timestamp). Timestamps are fixed-width ns
integers, so lexicographic filename order is timestamp order. Therefore:

- `_latest(dir, TYPE)` reads only the LAST matching dirent, falling back to the next-older on a
  parse failure - the same shape `latest_ticket_digest` already uses. 1 open per type per ticket.
- `claim()` arbitration needs only CLAIM events newer than the latest ENQUEUE, which are a
  contiguous suffix of the sorted names; walk newest-first and stop once a filename's timestamp
  prefix is `<=` the enqueue timestamp. Bounded by the contention window, not history.

This deletes nothing, renames nothing and writes nothing, so `docs/concurrency.md` invariant I1
and cross-clone union merges are untouched.

Also pin the implicit coupling the optimisation depends on: a test asserting that the filename
timestamp prefix equals the event body's `timestamp` field for an appended event. Without it a
future writer that names files differently would silently mis-reduce.

Scope note: this fixes the ASYMPTOTE (the opens term), not today's constant - `listdir`
dominates at current scale, so the gate will still breach 20 ms. Do not claim the budget breach
is resolved; that needs a separate lever (a store-level index, or a cheaper drain gate).

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/unit/test_ticket_digest_store.py -q`
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q` (the two-clone union-merge regression from be8a0c0595 must stay green)
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint && env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `reduce_ticket` opens at most one file per event type per ticket in the no-corruption case, proven by a test that counts `open` calls against a ticket dir seeded with many ENQUEUE/CLAIM/DONE events.
- [x] `claim()` arbitration reads only CLAIM events newer than the latest ENQUEUE, proven by a test that seeds pre-enqueue CLAIM events and asserts they are not opened.
- [x] A corrupt newest event file falls back to the next-older one, proven by a test that writes invalid JSON as the newest file and asserts the reduce still resolves.
- [x] A test asserts the appended event's filename timestamp prefix equals its body `timestamp` field, pinning the ordering assumption the suffix read depends on.
- [x] Existing claim/drain semantics are unchanged: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py -q` passes.
- [x] No event file is deleted or renamed by this change, verified by the diff touching no `os.unlink`/`os.remove`/`os.rename` call.
